subject: Nested PO approval lanes & invoice drip strategy for Q3 pilot
messages:
From: Linda Park <linda.park@nestbiotech.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nestahealth.com
Date: 2027-05-29T17:12:00-07:00
Subject: Purchase order format and billing gating for Q3 pilot

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Nest Biotech is excited to move the Q3 pilot forward. Procurement has a few specific constraints we need to resolve before legal will sign the SOW:

- Our ERP requires a single PO number per purchase, but we often route the value across multiple internal approval lanes (finance, lab ops). We need to ensure Redwood's invoice header maps to our nested approval tags (PO > sub-approval-id).
- Can Redwood accept a weekly invoice "drip" (multiple invoices that sum to the PO total) while keeping a single PO ID? Our AP team prefers weekly run invoices with a running balance, rather than a single monthly invoice.
- Net terms: our standard is Net60; would Redwood consider Net45 for the pilot, or a hybrid where the final invoice has Net60 while interim drip invoices are Net0 (for reconciliation)?

I attached our PO template (PO_Template_NestBiotech.pdf). Can you confirm what fields Redwood needs populated on the PO and whether you require any extra metadata (cost center, ledger tag) to map to your billing lanes?

If it helps, procurement can provision a temporary pre-authorized ledger tag for the pilot — we just need Redwood to show sample invoice line formatting for our AP team.

Next steps: can you respond with a recommended billing approach and sample invoice stub by Friday? We want to avoid back-and-forth during the legal review.

Best,
Linda Park
Senior Procurement Manager
Nest Biotech
procurement@nestahealth.com

Attachment: PO_Template_NestBiotech.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Linda Park <linda.park@nestbiotech.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Purchase order format and billing gating for Q3 pilot

Hi Linda — thanks for the clear list. Appreciate the template; our finance team reviewed it and I summarized three workable paths below with pros/cons so procurement and AP can pick the fit that causes the least ERP friction:

1) Single-PO with invoice-drip (recommended pilot)
   - Redwood invoices weekly against the same PO number. Each invoice includes a sub-header field "approval_lane" that matches your sub-approval-id. Running balance included on every invoice.
   - Pros: fast, matches your weekly cadence; avoids a large single invoice reconciliation.
   - Cons: requires your ERP to accept repeated invoices tied to one PO (most modern ERPs can, but some workflows flag duplicates).

2) Split PO per approval lane, aggregated in Redwood ledger
   - Procurement issues multiple PO numbers (one per approval lane); Redwood accepts multiple POs and aggregates to a single customer ledger number.
   - Pros: mirrors current approval structure; clean mapping in ERP.
   - Cons: requires procurement to issue multiple POs — more overhead on your side.

3) Monthly consolidated invoice (fallback)
   - Redwood issues a single invoice at month-end with line items tied to approval lanes.
   - Pros: simplest for Redwood billing; fewer invoices for AP.
   - Cons: not aligned to your preferred weekly run.

Net terms: we can accept Net45 for the pilot if procurement will agree to a 30-day evaluation and a documented exception in the SOW. For the invoice-drip option we can mark interim invoices Net0 and make the month-end reconciliation invoice Net45/Net60 as you prefer.

I attached a short proposal with example invoice stubs (Redwood_Billing_Options_Proposal.xlsx) and a sample PDF invoice we can send to your AP team.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm preferred path (1/2/3) by EOD Friday.
- If path 1, procurement confirms whether your ERP flags repeated invoice numbers; if so, we can switch to path 2.
- Redwood prepares SOW addendum with the agreed net terms and pilot exception for signature.

Cc'ing Vanessa (Sales Ops) and Ben (Finance) to coordinate SOW and any contract redline.

Thanks,
Markus
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Attachment: Redwood_Billing_Options_Proposal.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Linda Park <linda.park@nestbiotech.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nestahealth.com
Date: 2027-05-31T11:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Purchase order format and billing gating for Q3 pilot

Markus — thanks for the clear options. A few clarifications from our AP/ERP side:

- Our ERP (legacy instance) can accept repeated invoices under the same PO, but only if each invoice includes the sub-approval-id and a running-balance field; otherwise it triggers a duplicate detection flag.
- For legal reasons we cannot mark interim invoices Net0; every issued invoice must carry a payment term. That said, we can accept a staged schedule where interim invoices are Net30 and the final reconciliation invoice is Net60.
- Procurement can issue a single PO with nested approval tags. We'll attach our internal policy reference: "Nest Biotech PO Policy v3" for your legal/finance.

Can you produce a SampleInvoiceStub.pdf using the running-balance + sub-approval-id fields so we can validate with our ERP team? If that looks good we'll move to an internal procurement exception for Net45 for the pilot.

Thanks — Linda

Date: 2027-06-01T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Purchase order format and billing gating for Q3 pilot

Hi Linda,

Thanks for the ERP details — that helps. Ben and I dug into the fields your ERP requires and here's our recommended operational approach that minimizes manual work on both sides:

- Agree to Path 1 (Single-PO with invoice-drip) with the following constraints:
  * Each invoice will include: PO (primary), sub-approval-id (custom field), running_balance, and our internal ledger_tag.
  * Each invoice will carry Net30 for interim invoices and Net60 for the final reconciliation invoice (per your legal guidance). Redwood will accept that mix for the pilot.
- To mitigate duplicate detection we will prefix the invoice number with a sequence (e.g., NB-PO123-INV-001) and include the running_balance field as a required invoice attribute. That should satisfy your ERP duplicate heuristics.
- We will request procurement to issue a single PO with a temporary pre-authorized ledger tag. Procurement to send the PO and the ledger tag in a single PDF.

Operational asks for procurement/AP:
- Can procurement include the sub-approval-id as a searchable string in the PO PDF (exact text matching helps our ingestion).
- Please confirm the date range for weekly invoicing (which day you expect the run).

Ben, I'll create the SOW addendum with the Net45 concession clause (pilot-only) and the invoice sequencing requirement. Markus — once legal approves the wording we'll route a DocuSign envelope.

DocuSign link (draft): https://na1.docusign.net/embeddedSigning/ABC123456789
Jira for onboarding: JIRA-INC-8891
